opennyai_summary.PREAMBLE:
Munesh Agarwal vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023
Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma
Bench: Subhash Chandra Sharma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:111881
Court No. - 82
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 4792 of 2023
Applicant :- Munesh Agarwal
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Vishal Tandon Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the material placed on record.
This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No. 634 of 2018, under sections 420, 465, 468, 471 IPC and Section 3/7 of Essential Commodities Act and Section 66-D I.T. (Amendment) Act and Section 34 of Aadhar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act 2016, Police Station- Civil Lines, District- Muzaffar Nagar.
Further submitted co-accused Amit Kumar, Kanwarpal, Tarun Munesh Agarwal vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128946235/
1 Kumar, Masood Arif, Mukesh Kumar & Brajpal have already been granted anticipatory bail by coordinate Benches of this Court on 12.12.2022, 13.2.2023 & 24.02.2023 through Criminal Misc.
Anticipatory Bail Application Nos. 12561 of 2022, 1582 of 2023 & 13394 of 2022, since the role of present applicant is not distinguishable with the role of co-accused, the applicant is also entitled for bail.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is submitted by learned counsel for the that he is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
He has committed no offence.
Lastly, it is submitted that the applicant is under apprehension of imminent arrest.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In case, he is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the trial.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record an the fact that other co-accused persons have already been enlarged on bail by co-ordinate Benches of this Court and the case of the present applicant is on similar footing, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail during the pendency of trial.
In the event of arrest of the applicant- Munesh Agarwal, shall be released on anticipatory bail during pendency of trial on furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 25,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the learned trial court unless exempted;
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office;
(iii) The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if he has passport, the same shall be deposited by him before the S.S.P./S.P.
concerned.
In default of any of the conditions, this bail order shall stand automatically vacated.
